company: Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile (SQM)
market_holds: Spot $51.84 at the 18:08 UTC seal, 1.4% above the 52-week low and 45.6% below the 52-week high. Run-up is -4.8% over 5 sessions and -13.7% over 20 (sealed baseline). From the Oct 20 close to the Nov 17 intraday print SQM fell about 13.9%, against about -8.0% for ALB, about -12.1% for LIT and about -4.9% for SPY (Yahoo daily bars, own arithmetic), so the run-in is the lithium basket and not news about SQM. The front-week straddle implies 6.99%, or 6.0% net of ordinary volatility, but the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so that figure is only indicative. At the last four prints the opening gaps were +5.5% (Nov 2025), -4.0% (Feb/Mar 2026), -3.0% (May 2026) and +1.1% (Aug 2026), from Yahoo bars and the optionslam event dates. Consensus is $1.94 EPS and ~$2.26B revenue (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-10); another aggregator shows $2.02. Q2 was $2.31 and $2.47B. At Q2 (2026-08-19) the CEO guided Q3 lithium prices 'relatively stable' and volumes about flat at ~84kt. China battery-grade carbonate has collapsed: about 161k RMB at the start of Q3, 127.75k at end-Q3 (Benchmark), 99.35k on Oct 22, 91.7k on Nov 5 and ~90k on Nov 12 (SMM). Short interest is ~0.8% of float. The stock trades on the realized lithium price and what the CEO says in the release about next-quarter prices. The call is at 10:00 ET on Nov 18, after the scoring open, so only the release text counts in the window.
view: Q3 realized lithium price is the first line. Chile's central-bank lithium export price, which is close to what SQM actually receives, moved far less than China spot: $21,674/t in May, $20,825 in June, $19,368 in September and $17,513 for October to the 20th. SQM's Q2 realized price of $21.8/kg tracked that series. That puts Q3 Novandino realized near $19-20/kg, down 8-13%, which fits the CEO's 'relatively stable' guide. My own rebuild, with flat volume, intl spodumene ~$110M, the other segments ~$675M and ~60% pass-through at a ~39% tax rate, gives revenue of $2.23-2.30B and EPS of $2.00-2.10. That is in line with, to slightly above, the $1.94-2.02 consensus. It is not a gap I can trust: the arithmetic is coarse, and SQM missed EPS by 18-20% in Q4'25 and Q1'26 despite revenue beats before it beat by 13% in Q2. The second line is the Q4 language. The export price was already ~$17.5k in October and China spot is ~90k RMB, so Q4 realized is heading toward the mid-teens, perhaps 15-20% lower quarter on quarter. Albemarle has already said this out loud (2026-11-04: Q4 sales and EBITDA down sequentially), and the sector has sold off on it, with SQM at its 52-week low. Albemarle's print is the nearest read-across: a beat on a lowered bar plus a guide-down still gapped ALB +4.8% at the open. A beaten-down lithium name that prints 'less bad' can rally. Against that, SQM's own gaps have been small and two-sided, and the market can read a cut to the 2026 Novandino volume range (280-290kt) or soft Q4 volumes harshly. Net: a slight lean up from a probable in-line-to-better Q3 on a de-rated stock with sector-wide washout, but nowhere near a confident call.
unpriced: Possibly a small one. Analysts may be cutting Q3 off the China spot slide (-21% over Q3) when SQM's own realized price follows the much smoother Chilean export price (-7% June to September). That would make the Q3 headline land at or slightly above consensus. The size and reliability of that gap are too small to trade, and the Q4 outlook, which the market already discounts, is likely to dominate.

recommendation.reason: My rebuild from Chile's export-price series puts Q3 in line to slightly above the $1.94 consensus. The stock is washed out at its 52-week low, and Albemarle's guide-down print still gapped up. But SQM's EPS surprises have been erratic (two ~20% misses, then a 13% beat), and the release will carry a weaker Q4 price outlook. The edge is too small and too uncertain to clear 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Novandino realized price below ~$19/kg, or Q3 volumes well below 84kt with a cut to the 2026 280-290kt range, would make it a down print. A realized price near $20/kg with the volume range reaffirmed would strengthen the up lean.

self_critique: The Chile export-price series comes second-hand, via a newspaper's reading of central-bank data, and July and August are missing. SQM's realized price may track China spot more closely than I assume, because a large share of its volume goes to China on short-lag index pricing; if so, Q3 realized could be ~$18/kg and the print a miss. Its EPS has been erratic on costs, CORFO and taxes. The release's Q4 language will point to a sharply lower realized price, and a reduced volume outlook would hit a stock that trades on the forward price rather than the quarter.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was useful: the 20-day fall is the sector, so it only sets the bar. Rebuilding the line from the Chilean export price (P3, own arithmetic) gave the only real lead. P7's push to estimate the line was sensible here, but the company's erratic surprise record kept it short of a recommendation.
